confirmed_blocking.summary: The run's own committed state carries a hand-edited history event 'halted' that the delivered closed-vocabulary validator refuses, so every writer command on this run fails and no shipped tool can repair the file.
confirmed_blocking.evidence: Reproduced: state.validate_state on the committed file returns history[11].event "'halted' is off-vocabulary" (state.py:38). The entry was hand-written in commit 79e0bf9. write_state validates before upgrade() (state.py:381 vs 395), so the run cannot checkpoint, verify, set-status or resume, and there is no repair command. data-model.md:34 and contracts/cli.md:36 name the conformant representation: 'halted' is a status with halt_reason; only aborted/pr-open write history events. ENG-26, ENG-17.
confirmed_blocking.fix: Either rewrite history[11] to the conformant shape (drop the 'halted' event; keep status/halt_reason) or deliberately extend the vocabulary in data-model.md, state.md and HISTORY_EVENTS together; and give the validator a documented legacy tolerance or ship a repair command.

confirmed_blocking.summary: The FR-015 personal-model pipeline is wrong in both directions: render.py merges ${FACTORY_HOME}/config.json only when FACTORY_HOME is exported (the documented default ~/.factory is ignored), so overrides never reach the installed agents and the --models report misreports effective models, while an exported FACTORY_HOME makes install.sh's two render.py calls re-render the committed dist/ with personal model ids.
confirmed_blocking.evidence: install.sh:44 and :55 invoke render.py, whose render() rmtrees and rewrites the committed dist (render.py:100-152). load_adapter merges config only when FACTORY_HOME is set (render.py:43-47) while README.md:23-29 documents ${FACTORY_HOME:-~/.factory}/config.json; the render.py:44 comment is false; test_render_models.py:121-141 asserts the default home is ignored. Demonstrated in a sandbox both ways. FR-015 not met; round-1 STD-9/SEC-2 unfixed.
confirmed_blocking.fix: Make install.sh report effective models by reading the user's factory home without rendering the linked dist; unset FACTORY_HOME for canonical renders; correct the render.py comment; add an install-seam assertion covering the default home.
